coffea-arabica.name: Coffea arabica
coffea-arabica.summary: The species of coffee plant believed to have been cultivated first, making up about 60% of global coffee production and native to the highlands of Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Yemen.

harar.name: Harar
harar.summary: Walled city in eastern Ethiopia, a long-standing trading hub linking the Horn of Africa to Arabia and beyond, called by UNESCO the 'fourth holiest city' of Islam.

ethiopia-commodity-exchange.name: Ethiopia Commodity Exchange
ethiopia-commodity-exchange.summary: A commodities exchange established in Ethiopia in 2008 to modernize the trading of goods like coffee, growing rapidly to reach $1.1 billion in value by 2011.

national-coffee-association.name: National Coffee Association
national-coffee-association.summary: The main U.S. trade association for the coffee industry, handling market research, lobbying and public relations on its behalf.

irgachefe.name: Irgachefe
irgachefe.summary: A town in central southern Ethiopia's Gedeo Zone, administrative center of an important coffee-growing district, with a population of about 21,000 as of 2005.

tigray-region.name: Tigray Region
tigray-region.summary: The northernmost regional state of Ethiopia, homeland of the Tigrayan, Irob and Kunama peoples, with Mekelle as its capital.

wollo-province.name: Wollo
wollo-province.summary: A historical province of northern Ethiopia, known in the Middle Ages as Bete Amhara and the centre of the Solomonic dynasty founded around Lake Hayq in 1270.

somali-ostrich.name: Somali ostrich
somali-ostrich.summary: A large flightless bird native to the Horn of Africa, recognized as a species distinct from the common ostrich only in 2014; long partly domesticated by Somalis.

lalibela.name: Lalibela
lalibela.summary: A town in Ethiopia's Amhara Region famed for rock-cut monolithic churches traditionally dated to the reign of King Gebre Meskel Lalibela (r. c. 1181-1221); one of Ethiopia's holiest pilgrimage sites.

amhara-region.name: Amhara Region
amhara-region.summary: A regional state in northern Ethiopia, homeland of the Amhara and other peoples, containing Lake Tana, the source of the Blue Nile, and Ethiopia's highest peak.

ethiopia-museum-of-art-and-science.name: Ethiopia Museum of Art and Science
ethiopia-museum-of-art-and-science.summary: A 15,000-square-metre science museum in Addis Ababa inaugurated in 2022 by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, featuring exhibition halls and a circular building nicknamed the "ring of wisdom".
ethiopia-museum-of-art-and-science.source_title: Ethiopia Museum of Art and Science

abiy-ahmed.name: Abiy Ahmed
abiy-ahmed.summary: Ethiopian politician born in 1976, prime minister of Ethiopia and leader of the Prosperity Party since 2019, awarded the 2019 Nobel Peace Prize for resolving the border conflict with Eritrea.

ge-ez.name: Ge'ez
ge-ez.summary: Ancient South Semitic language from Ethiopia and Eritrea, still used today as the liturgical language of Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox and Catholic churches.

ogaden.name: Ogaden
ogaden.summary: A plateau region in eastern Ethiopia inhabited mainly by Somalis, marked by over a century of self-determination movements following Ethiopian annexation in the 1890s.

western-somali-liberation-front.name: Western Somali Liberation Front
western-somali-liberation-front.summary: A Somali nationalist movement that fought for the independence of the Ogaden region from Ethiopia and its union with Somalia, playing a central role in the 1977-78 Ogaden War.

derg.name: Derg
derg.summary: The military junta that ruled Ethiopia from 1974 to 1991 after overthrowing Emperor Haile Selassie, abolishing the monarchy and, under Mengistu Haile Mariam, waging the deadly Red Terror campaign.

haile-selassie.name: Haile Selassie
haile-selassie.summary: Emperor of Ethiopia from 1930 to 1974, born Tafari Makonnen; he introduced modernizing reforms, led Ethiopia through Italian occupation, and is revered as divine in Rastafari.

second-italo-ethiopian-war.name: Second Italo-Ethiopian War
second-italo-ethiopian-war.summary: Italy's invasion of Ethiopia from 1935 to 1936, regarded as the largest colonial campaign in history, in which Mussolini authorized the use of mustard gas against Ethiopian forces.

axum.name: Axum
axum.summary: A town in Ethiopia's Tigray Region, once capital of the ancient Aksumite Empire, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980 for its archaeological importance.

adwa.name: Adwa
adwa.summary: Town in Ethiopia's Tigray Region, best known as the site near the 1896 Battle of Adwa, where Ethiopian forces defeated Italian troops.

red-terror-ethiopia.name: Qey Shibir (Red Terror)
red-terror-ethiopia.summary: A violent political repression campaign by Ethiopia's Derg government against rival Marxist-Leninist groups from 1976 to 1978, estimated to have killed between 10,000 and 980,000 people.

mengistu-haile-mariam.name: Mengistu Haile Mariam
mengistu-haile-mariam.summary: An Ethiopian communist revolutionary who led the Derg military junta from 1977 to 1987 and served as head of state until 1991, overseeing the violent Red Terror crackdown.

jijiga.name: Jijiga
jijiga.summary: Capital city of Ethiopia's Somali Region, near the border with Somaliland, becoming the region's capital in 1995 after replacing Gode.

tigray-people-s-liberation-front.name: Tigray People's Liberation Front
tigray-people-s-liberation-front.summary: A Tigrayan ethnic nationalist and paramilitary group founded in 1975 that led Ethiopia's ruling coalition from 1991 to 2018.

eritrean-people-s-liberation-front.name: Eritrean People's Liberation Front
eritrean-people-s-liberation-front.summary: A Marxist–Leninist Eritrean liberation movement that split from the ELF in 1973 and led the fight that won Eritrea's independence from Ethiopia in 1991.

yemodish-bekele.name: Yemodish Bekele
yemodish-bekele.summary: Ethiopian author (1960-2025) of thirteen books, the first Ethiopian woman to publish her own short story collection, and a women's rights activist who led several organizations.

my-life-and-ethiopia-s-progress.name: My Life and Ethiopia's Progress
my-life-and-ethiopia-s-progress.summary: The autobiography of Emperor Haile Selassie I of Ethiopia, written over his lifetime and published in two volumes in 1973-74.

edward-ullendorff.name: Edward Ullendorff
edward-ullendorff.summary: British scholar (1920–2011) of Semitic languages and Ethiopian studies.

lij-iyasu.name: Lij Iyasu
lij-iyasu.summary: Designated Emperor of Ethiopia from 1913 to 1916, never formally crowned; baptismal name Kifle Yaqob, born 1895, died 1935.

zewditu.name: Zewditu
zewditu.summary: Empress of Ethiopia from 1916 to 1930, the empire's only reigning empress, crowned in 1917 and known for conservative policies resisting the modernizing reforms of her regent, later Emperor Haile Selassie I.

zewde-gebre-sellassie.name: Zewde Gebre-Sellassie
zewde-gebre-sellassie.summary: Ethiopian nobleman, historian and former Deputy Prime Minister of Ethiopia (1926–2008), born in the village of Galdu near Addis Ababa.

musa-haji-ismail-galal.name: Musa Haji Ismail Galal
musa-haji-ismail-galal.summary: Somali polymath (1917–1980) active as a writer, scholar, linguist, poet, historian, anthropologist and meteorologist, known for creating the Galaal script for Somali.

population-media-center.name: Population Media Center
population-media-center.summary: An educational entertainment organization based in Vermont, dedicated to women's rights, population stabilization and the environment.

addis-ababa-university.name: Addis Ababa University
addis-ababa-university.summary: Ethiopia's oldest and national university, based in Addis Ababa with a further campus in Bishoftu, admitting students through the national university entrance exam.

haramaya-university.name: Haramaya University
haramaya-university.summary: Public research university in Haramaya, Oromia Region, Ethiopia, about 5 km west of Harar and 510 km east of Addis Ababa.

ambo-university.name: Ambo University
ambo-university.summary: A national university in Ambo, Ethiopia, established by government proclamation in 2011.

jimma-university.name: Jimma University
jimma-university.summary: A public research university in Jimma, Ethiopia, ranked the country's leading university for four straight years (2009–2012), formed in 1999 from the merger of Jimma College of Agriculture (founded 1952) and Jimma Institute of Health Sciences (founded 1983).

mekelle-university.name: Mekelle University
mekelle-university.summary: A public university in Mekelle, Ethiopia, one of the country's largest, with seven colleges and over 90 undergraduate programs.

ministry-of-science-and-higher-education.name: Ministry of Science and Higher Education (Ethiopia)
ministry-of-science-and-higher-education.summary: An Ethiopian government department (2018–2021) overseeing science, higher education and technical and vocational training, later merged into the Ministry of Education.
ministry-of-science-and-higher-education.source_title: Ministry of Science and Higher Education (Ethiopia)

hirut-woldemariam.name: Hirut Woldemariam
hirut-woldemariam.summary: An Ethiopian writer, teacher and politician, born 1975, who served as a government minister for science and higher education and was the first woman to be vice president of Addis Ababa University.

solomonic-dynasty.name: Solomonic dynasty
solomonic-dynasty.summary: Ruling dynasty of the Ethiopian Empire from the 13th to 20th centuries, founded in 1270 by Yekuno Amlak and claiming descent from the biblical Solomon; ended in 1974 with Haile Selassie's overthrow.

italian-eritrea.name: Italian Eritrea
italian-eritrea.summary: Italy's colony in present-day Eritrea, officially founded in 1890 after decades of territorial expansion, lasting until Italy lost the region during World War II in 1941.

oromo-liberation-front.name: Oromo Liberation Front
oromo-liberation-front.summary: An Oromo nationalist political party formed in 1973 to seek self-determination and independence for the Oromo people of Ethiopia.

tigray-war.name: Tigray war
tigray-war.summary: A civil war from November 2020 to November 2022 fought in Ethiopia's Tigray Region between federal and Eritrean forces and the TPLF.

organisation-of-african-unity.name: Organisation of African Unity
organisation-of-african-unity.summary: An African organization founded in 1963 to promote unity and end colonialism, dissolved in 2002 and replaced by the African Union.

federation-of-ethiopia-and-eritrea.name: Federation of Ethiopia and Eritrea
federation-of-ethiopia-and-eritrea.summary: A 1952–1962 union between the former Italian colony of Eritrea and the Ethiopian Empire, created after Italy renounced its African territories under the 1947 Treaty of Paris.

ketema-yifru.name: Ketema Yifru
ketema-yifru.summary: An Ethiopian diplomat and statesman (1929–1994) who helped found the Organization of African Unity in 1963 and shaped Ethiopian foreign policy in the late Imperial era.

imperial-parliament-of-ethiopia.name: Chamber of Deputies (Ethiopia)
imperial-parliament-of-ethiopia.summary: Lower house of the Imperial Parliament of Ethiopia, which existed from 1931 to 1974; the 1955 constitution introduced elections to it.

people-s-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia.name: People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
people-s-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia.summary: A communist state in Ethiopia and Eritrea from 1987 to 1991, led by Mengistu Haile Mariam after the ruling Derg junta adopted a new constitution.

workers-party-of-ethiopia.name: Workers' Party of Ethiopia
workers-party-of-ethiopia.summary: A Marxist-Leninist party that ruled Ethiopia from 1984 to 1991 under General Secretary Mengistu Haile Mariam, founded by the Derg and the sole legal party from 1987.

national-palace-addis-ababa.name: Jubilee Palace
national-palace-addis-ababa.summary: Formerly known as Jubilee Palace, this Addis Ababa residence housed Emperor Haile Selassie until the 1974 coup and later became an official residence for Ethiopia's president.

holy-trinity-cathedral-addis-ababa.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral, Addis Ababa
holy-trinity-cathedral-addis-ababa.summary: The highest-ranking Ethiopian Orthodox cathedral in Addis Ababa, built under Emperor Haile Selassie and completed in 1942 to commemorate Ethiopia's victory over Italian occupation.

julius-nyerere.name: Julius Nyerere
julius-nyerere.summary: Tanzanian politician and political theorist (1922–1999) who led Tanganyika to independence in 1961. He was president of Tanzania from 1964 to 1985 and a founder of the TANU party.

ujamaa.name: Ujamaa
ujamaa.summary: Socialist ideology behind Julius Nyerere's development policies in Tanzania after independence in 1961. More broadly it can mean cooperative economics, and Maulana Karenga adopted it as a principle of Kwanzaa.

hatata.name: Hatata
hatata.summary: Two 17th-century Geʽez philosophical treatises on reason and ethics from Ethiopia, written by Zara Yaqob and his patron's son Walda Heywat, first translated into English in 2023.

carlo-conti-rossini.name: Carlo Conti Rossini
carlo-conti-rossini.summary: An Italian orientalist (1872–1949) who directed the State Treasury and belonged to the Accademia dei Lincei and Royal Academy of Italy, best known for his works on the historical geography of Ethiopia.

giusto-da-urbino.name: Giusto da Urbino
giusto-da-urbino.summary: An Italian Capuchin missionary to Ethiopia and linguist (1814–1856), known in Ge'ez as Abba Yostos.

zera-yacob-philosopher.name: Zera Yacob
zera-yacob-philosopher.summary: Ethiopian philosopher (1600–1693) who, while exiled in a cave, wrote the Hatata, arguing for reason and religious tolerance over blind faith in Church dogma.

ethiopian-orthodox-tewahedo-church.name: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church
ethiopian-orthodox-tewahedo-church.summary: The largest Oriental Orthodox church, tracing back to the Christianization of Aksum in 330 CE, with tens of millions of adherents and one of only a few Oriental Orthodox churches in Africa.

coptic-orthodox-church.name: Coptic Orthodox Church
coptic-orthodox-church.summary: An Oriental Orthodox Christian church based in Egypt, traditionally founded by Saint Mark around AD 42, and the largest Christian group in Egypt and the Middle East.

pope-cyril-vi-of-alexandria.name: Pope Cyril VI
pope-cyril-vi-of-alexandria.summary: Born Azer Youssef Atta, the 116th Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the Coptic Church from 1959 until his death in 1971.

beta-israel.name: Beta Israel
beta-israel.summary: Jewish community originating in the Amhara and Tigray regions of northern Ethiopia, historically practicing a distinct non-Talmudic form of Judaism; most have emigrated to Israel since 1979.

law-of-return.name: Law of Return
law-of-return.summary: An Israeli law, passed in 1950 and extended in 1970, giving Jews and their descendants the right to immigrate to and become citizens of Israel.

eugen-mittwoch.name: Eugen Mittwoch
eugen-mittwoch.summary: A German-Jewish scholar (1876–1942) who founded modern Islamic studies in Germany and served as Berlin director of the American Jewish Joint Distribution Committee.

claude-sumner.name: Claude Sumner
claude-sumner.summary: Canadian professor of philosophy at Addis Ababa University from 1953, best known for his work on the Ethiopian philosopher Zera Yacob; died 2012.

getatchew-haile.name: Getatchew Haile
getatchew-haile.summary: Ethiopian-American philologist (1931–2021) considered the foremost scholar of the Ge'ez language, honoured with a MacArthur "genius" award.

benito-mussolini.name: Benito Mussolini
benito-mussolini.summary: Italian dictator (1883–1945) who founded fascism and led Italy from 1922 until his overthrow in 1943; executed by the Italian resistance in 1945.

michael-manley.name: Michael Manley
michael-manley.summary: Jamaican politician, trade unionist and journalist who served as Jamaica's fourth prime minister, from 1972 to 1980 and 1989 to 1992, championing democratic socialism.

bah-faith.name: Baháʼí Faith
bah-faith.summary: A religion founded by Baháʼu'lláh in 19th-century Iran teaching the unity of all religions and people, with 7 to 8 million followers worldwide today.

abdu-l-bah.name: ʻAbdu'l-Bahá
abdu-l-bah.summary: Eldest son of Baháʼu'lláh, founder of the Baháʼí Faith, and its head from 1892 to 1921 as one of its three central figures; imprisoned for decades before later traveling west to spread the faith.

spiritual-assembly.name: Spiritual Assembly
spiritual-assembly.summary: An elected council that governs the Baháʼí Faith at the local or national level, since the religion has no clergy.

pope-benedict-xv.name: Pope Benedict XV
pope-benedict-xv.summary: Head of the Catholic Church from 1914 to 1922, whose papacy focused on World War I; he declared Vatican neutrality and led humanitarian relief efforts.

st-stephen-of-the-abyssinians.name: St. Stephen of the Abyssinians
st-stephen-of-the-abyssinians.summary: An Ethiopian Catholic chapel in Vatican City and the national church of Ethiopia, one of the few structures there to survive the demolition of Old St. Peter's Basilica around 1505.

p-ent-ay.name: P'ent'ay
p-ent-ay.summary: An Amharic-Tigrinya term for Pentecostal Christians, now used for all Evangelical Protestant denominations in Ethiopian and Eritrean societies.

mahmoud-ahmed.name: Mahmoud Ahmed
mahmoud-ahmed.summary: Ethiopian singer, born in 1941, who became widely popular in Ethiopia in the 1970s and later gained international fame among fans in Europe and the Americas.

tilahun-gessesse.name: Tilahun Gessesse
tilahun-gessesse.summary: Ethiopian tenor (1940–2009) nicknamed 'The Voice', a leading singer of his country's 1960s 'Golden Age' who also raised money for famine relief.

alemayehu-eshete.name: Alemayehu Eshete
alemayehu-eshete.summary: An Ethiopian singer (1941-2021) nicknamed the 'Abyssinian Elvis', known for blending Ethiopian music with rock and roll and for hits like Temar Lije, later reaching wider fame through the Éthiopiques recordings.

mulatu-astatke.name: Mulatu Astatke
mulatu-astatke.summary: Ethiopian musician and arranger, born in 1943, considered the father of 'Ethio-jazz', who introduced instruments such as the vibraphone and conga drums into Ethiopian popular music.

ethio-jazz.name: Ethio-jazz
ethio-jazz.summary: A genre blending traditional Ethiopian pentatonic melodies with jazz, originating in the 1950s and revolutionized in the 1960s by Mulatu Astatke, considered its father.

kingdom-of-aksum.name: Kingdom of Aksum
kingdom-of-aksum.summary: A powerful trading kingdom in the Horn of Africa and South Arabia, founded around the 1st century, ranked among the era's four great powers, and one of the first states to adopt Christianity, in the 4th century.

amha-records.name: Amha Records
amha-records.summary: An Ethiopian record label founded by Amha Eshete that released 103 singles and 12 albums between 1969 and 1975, recording prominent Ethiopian singers and musicians.

kaifa-records.name: Kaifa Records
kaifa-records.summary: Ethiopian record label that released 53 records between 1973 and 1977, recording singers such as Alemayehu Eshete and Mahmoud Ahmed.

buda-musique.name: Buda Musique
buda-musique.summary: French record label specializing in world music, founded in 1987, known for its Éthiopiques series compiling Ethiopian recordings.

operation-moses.name: Operation Moses
operation-moses.summary: Covert 1984 evacuation of Ethiopian Jews from Sudan during a civil war and famine, originally named 'Cub of the Lion of Judah' before being renamed by the United Jewish Appeal.

operation-joshua.name: Operation Joshua
operation-joshua.summary: 1985 airlift of Ethiopian Jewish refugees from Sudan to Israel, arranged after Sudan halted earlier flights; roughly 500 to 650 people were flown out on US Air Force transport planes.

operation-solomon.name: Operation Solomon
operation-solomon.summary: Covert 1991 Israeli airlift that flew 14,325 Ethiopian Jews to Israel in 36 hours aboard 35 aircraft, following the earlier Operations Moses and Joshua.

jinka.name: Jinka
jinka.summary: Market town in the hills of southern Ethiopia, capital of the Ari Zone and a center for at least sixteen indigenous ethnic groups.

operation-tzur-israel.name: Operation Tzur Israel
operation-tzur-israel.summary: Israeli government initiative from 2020 to 2023 that brought about 5,000 members of the Ethiopian Jewish community, mostly people left out of earlier immigration waves, to Israel.
